HSV-2 is less common in extragenital sites but possible via autoinoculation or atypical reactivation. VZV is plausible given dermatomal vesicles and facial pain, though zoster typically spares the forearm if trigeminal is involved unless there’s multidermatomal spread; the absence of classic rash in the trigeminal distribution lowers confidence slightly. Secondary syphilis can cause mucocutaneous blisters and systemic symptoms including headache or cranial neuropathy, but dyspareunia is nonspecific and vesicular forearm lesions are uncommon; serology would be needed to rule out. Ramsay Hunt is less likely without ear pain, vesicles in the external auditory canal, or facial palsy—but facial pain with cranial nerve involvement warrants inclusion.
